title: Adaptive context-slicing and quantized fallback orchestration for OOM resiliency
creator: Asha Patel
description: Short summary: Implement a runtime control loop that prevents GPU OOMs by dynamically slicing request context into smaller 'slabs', performing on-the-fly per-request quantized execution of less-critical segments, compacting KV cache heuristically, and orchestrating fallback model swaps with progressive retries. Focus is to keep high-priority tokens served at full fidelity while gracefully degrading low-importance context and preserving latency SLOs where possible.
background: We've seen intermittent GPU OOMs for long-context requests with heavy KV cache occupancy during peak bursts. Current mitigations (static eviction, coarse-grained fallback to smaller models) either cause high user-visible regressions or are too slow to prevent OOMs in the hot path.

This ticket prototypes a combined approach: 1) admission/control to avoid instant OOMs, 2) context-slicing that isolates hot KV entries and low-importance prefixes, 3) opportunistic quantized execution and micro-model switchover for degraded segments, and 4) fast recoverable retries with KV rehydration.
design_decisions: Prefer non-blocking context slicing to avoid tail latency cliffs: slice into overlapping slabs with prioritized processing order.
Quantization is applied to slab segments only; core prompt and last-k tokens remain full precision to preserve output fidelity.
KV compaction uses LRU-weighted scoring with recency boost for tokens currently in active generation sessions.
Fallback micro-models must be warm in a small pool (CPU or smaller GPU) to keep retry latency under 120ms additional for degraded tokens.
Admission controller will use a token-based headroom estimator rather than raw memory usage to avoid tight coupling to specific GPU allocators.
implementation_notes: Runtime: extend batch admission to compute per-request 'slab_plan' (list of (start,end,priority) strings); slab_plan generated by new context analyzer module.
KV cache: introduce compressed-entry path (segmented quantized storage) and a 'hotset' ledger for active requests.
Execution: add runtime mode 'mixed-fidelity' supporting sub-request quantization flags and micro-model routing.
Scheduler: implement preemptible slab queues; high-priority slabs get earlier kernel scheduling and direct KV pinning.
Fallback: add model-routing policy 'progressive-degrade' which tries quantized slab, then micro-model, then full-request retry.
APIs/Config: new fields in route config: max_context_slices (int), slab_priority_threshold (float), quantize_max_slab_size (int), fallback_pools (list) - expose via console controls.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for slab_plan generator with synthetic contexts and expected slab boundaries.
Integration tests that simulate a bursting workload causing previous OOMs but now complete with no fatal OOM (end-to-end infra test).
E2E latency regression < 10% for P95 on signaling workloads compared to baseline when not degraded.
Quality regression: BLEU/ROUGE style evals on degraded outputs should show <= 5% drop on synthetic prompts where degradation is acceptable.
Monitoring: dashboard surfaces per-route 'degrade_rate' and 'oom_sentinel_triggers' and alert at >0 occurrences in staging; zero in canary.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12 — Spike: implemented slab_plan prototype in Python; generated reasonable slabs for multi-thousand token contexts. Trade-off: overlapping slabs simplify prefix fidelity but increase KV operations.
2026-02-16 — Design review with runtime leads: agreed to prefer on-host quantization of slabs to avoid remote copy latency. Action: add compressed KV entry layout.
2026-02-20 — PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/6789 implementing admission controller and slab scheduler (WIP).
2026-02-25 — Integration run in staging: prevented 3/3 OOM reproductions on synthetic replay; observed 15% additional per-request CPU for quantization, acceptable for canary.
risks: Quantizing slabs may introduce subtle generation artifacts especially for tasks sensitive to token embeddings alignment.
Maintaining warm micro-model pools increases steady-state cost; need autoscale policies tied to degrade_rate.
Complexity in KV compaction could lead to incorrect rehydration if versioning not handled carefully.
mitigations: Add conservative quantization profiles and run A/B on quality-critical customer prompts before wide rollout.
Autoscale micro-model pool based on moving average of degrade_rate and cap monthly burn.
Implement KV entry version and tombstone markers; add unit tests for rehydration correctness.
qa_plan: Synthetic OOM replay harness with variable inter-arrival times and long contexts.
Fuzzing on slab boundaries to ensure no token duplication or loss.
Quality evaluation: run standard regression prompts and compare with baseline for hallucination or coherence metrics.
rollout_plan: Canary (runtime-1.22-canary): enable on 1% traffic of a low-risk shard for 48h with strict monitoring.
If canary stable (no increase in P99 latency >5%, no customer-impactful quality regressions), expand to 10% over 72h.
Full rollout gated on cost-signals: micro-model pool expense must be <15% uplift vs baseline or compensated by reduced retry costs.
observability_metrics: degrade_rate (per-route) — fraction of requests using any degrade path
oom_sentinels — count of OOM preemption events
fallback_swap_rate — how often micro-model used for slab
p95_extra_latency_on_degrade_ms — additional latency introduced by degrade path
notes: Follow-ups: ops runbook for manual rollback, add per-customer opt-outs.
